clue.text: Recognise there's tidy fine for molesting

indicators.note: molesting the words disturbs and roughs them up, so their letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a tidy fine is due for someone caught molesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for molesting' is the anagram signal working on TIDY and FINE together; 'there's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify something is to recognise it and say what it is, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Characteristic of a single person

definitions.meaning: relating to one person alone rather than a group

explanation.definitionFit: Individual means both distinctive in character and belonging to one person only.

clue.text: Some food — does one have it before sham chicken, or not?

definitions.text: Some food — does one have it before sham chicken, or not?

parts.words: Some food — does one have it before sham chicken, or not?
parts.note: the old riddle of which came first, the hen or what it lays, dressed as a question about a meal

explanation.definitionFit: An egg is a food, and is the other half of the chicken-or-egg puzzle about which came first.

clue.text: Plant often considered a weed

parts.note: weed is a slang word for a smokeable leaf, so the plant is the one people call the weed

explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is a plant, and 'the weed' is an old slang term for it.

clue.text: Cheats over credit, initially sound? Rubbish!

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the next

parts.note: fiddles means cheats, as in fiddling the books
tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Swindlers get one over on the lender: does it sound fine? Nonsense!
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the cheats sit on top of the credit. 'Tick' meaning credit is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an old-fashioned exclamation meaning nonsense, the same as crying rubbish.

clue.text: Source of spin evident in reported speech

indicators.note: reported speech is something heard, so the word for speech is taken as it sounds

parts.note: talk means speech

explanation.surface: Political spin is betrayed in what someone is quoted as saying.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent TALK and TORQUE sound the same. 'evident in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Torque is the turning force that makes something rotate, so it is literally what causes spin.

clue.text: Visionary healer is found in old religion

indicators.note: the word is is found inside the religion, one placed within the other

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect

explanation.surface: A mystic faith-healer turns up in an ancient sect.
explanation.definitionFit: An oculist is an eye doctor, a healer concerned with vision.

clue.text: All the clubs, for example, where only naval officers may go

definitions.meaning: one of the four suits makes up a quarter of a pack of cards

definitions.text: where only naval officers may go
definitions.meaning: the part of a warship's upper deck reserved for officers

explanation.definitionFit: A quarterdeck is the officers' deck of a ship, and the clubs form a quarter of a card deck.

clue.text: Peaceful flat

explanation.definitionFit: Even means both calm and steady in temper and level or smooth in surface.

clue.text: Menial follows with trunk

parts.note: dogs means follows closely, as in dogging someone's steps
the trunk is the body, the torso without head and limbs

explanation.surface: A servant trails along behind carrying a trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody is a drudge given the menial jobs, so the noun equals a menial.

clue.text: Benevolent chap kept in the shade

indicators.note: the chap is kept inside the shade, one word placed within another

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A kindly fellow stays indoors out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a man resting out of the sun, but 'the shade' is a colour, not shadow, and the chap sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means showing kindness and compassion, a synonym of benevolent.

clue.text: Part of vintage car working, a pig to decoke at first

parts.note: running means working, as a machine is running
a boar is a male pig

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An old motor is going, but stripping carbon from it is a pig of a job.
explanation.walkthrough: To decoke an engine is to clean carbon from it; 'a' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A running board is the footboard along the side of old cars, a part of a vintage car.

clue.text: Wine-grower transforms university — turns it civil

indicators.note: to transform something is to change its shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A vintner changes a university, making it more polite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' looks like a second indicator but is fodder: U plus TURNS, IT and CIVIL are rearranged by 'transforms'.
explanation.definitionFit: A viniculturist cultivates grapes for wine-making, so is a wine-grower.

clue.text: The EU aims to transcend this turning out of Estonian tat

definitions.text: The EU aims to transcend this

indicators.note: turning out signals the letters turned about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Brussels hopes to move beyond the cheap souvenirs from Estonia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out of' rearranges ESTONIAN and TAT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation state is a sovereign country, the unit European integration seeks to go beyond.

clue.text: Leave to do recordings

explanation.definitionFit: To make tracks is slang for leaving, and literally means producing recorded songs.

clue.text: It's said in France to mean the same

parts.note: dit is French for said
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a French word means exactly the same thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'mean' are links joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to mean the same again, as on a list where a mark repeats what is above.

clue.text: Treatment centres appeal to military group, having fresh air

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal
NATO is the North Atlantic military alliance

indicators.note: fresh signals the letters made new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Clinics seek support from an army unit, with plenty of fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges AIR into RIA; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanatoria, plural of sanatorium, are institutions where patients receive treatment and convalesce.

clue.text: A function helping worship

parts.note: a do is a party or social function
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: A ceremony that assists religious devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and reverence, a synonym of worship.

clue.text: Holding up drink, I see last of The win Chardonnay wasting

indicators.note: holding means the exclamation holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: ah is what one says on understanding, I see

indicators.note: in a down clue up reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: port is a fortified drink

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to a prize won while the Chardonnay runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PORT into TROP, held in AH; the Y is the last letter of Chardonnay. 'The win' reads as an OCR slip for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is the wasting away of a body part or tissue.

clue.text: European announcement of opposing players' marriage?

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so what follows is taken as it sounds

parts.note: South and West are opponents at the bridge table; say S, W wed

explanation.surface: A notice that two rival sportspeople have married.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North and South play against East and West, so S and W are opposing players; 'S W wed' said quickly gives the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a person from Sweden, so a European.

clue.text: Cover in case he hates to move

indicators.note: to move the letters is to shift them into a different order

explanation.surface: He loathes being moved, so protects himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe is to put a blade into its sheath, covering it in a case.

clue.text: One who is not out to assault Luddite

parts.note: to strike is to hit or assault
the Luddites were workers who smashed machines, so a Luddite is a machine breaker

explanation.surface: A batsman still in is told to attack a technophobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not out' sounds like cricket but here means not out on strike; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A strikebreaker keeps working during a strike instead of walking out with colleagues.

clue.text: Legendary mountain in Ross and Cro-evan

indicators.note: in signals that the answer lies inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A mythical peak somewhere in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Ross and Cromarty is a former Scottish county; the run sits inside 'Ross and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the Greek mountain the giants piled on Pelion in myth.

clue.text: Son affected by one sort of seafood

parts.note: camp means affected or exaggerated in manner
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boy is put off by a particular dish from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' reads as 'made ill by' but gives CAMP, meaning mannered; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines, usually served breaded, a type of seafood.

clue.text: Two sailors I caught being sort of acid …

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
a second tar, another sailor
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A pair of seamen and I were caught out by some acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartaric acid is the acid found in grapes and wine, so it is a kind of acid.

clue.text: No time for genuine repentance

indicators.note: no time means T, the abbreviation for time, is taken away

parts.note: true means genuine

explanation.surface: Someone too busy to be truly sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue is regret or sorrow for something done, so it means repentance.

clue.text: … and their selfish-sounding compliance

indicators.note: sounding tells us to take the sailors' reply as it is heard

parts.note: the two sailors of the previous clue each saying I, I, a selfish-seeming reply

explanation.surface: The two sailors' obedience sounds rather self-centred.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on from 23 across: 'their' is the two sailors, whose naval reply sounds like 'I, I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aye aye is the naval acknowledgement of an order, so it expresses compliance.

clue.text: Exotic isle ends unemployment

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, signalling the letters taken out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Joblessness on a faraway island at the end of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is the state of having no work, a sense that overlaps with unemployment.
